journeys.title: Banda Islands by working passenger ship
journeys.feasibility: provisionally viable for October-November 2027 if the Ambon-Banda crossing has a fallback

season.note: Dive operators: high season Sep-Dec, mid Mar-Apr, low Jan/Feb/May/Aug, closed Jun-Jul (S8); best Sep-Dec (S9).

journeys.pull: About ten days in October or November: cross the Banda Sea from Ambon by ship or fast boat, stay six nights on Banda Neira, and take small boats to Banda Besar, Ai and Run. Mornings go to a reef that grew on a 1988 lava flow, afternoons to the history that made these islands the world's only source of nutmeg. Dive operators' high season, September to December, falls inside the friends' 2027 window S8 S9.
journeys.journey: Spine: fly to Jakarta or Bali, then to Ambon, then cross to Banda Neira for six nights with boat days, then return by boat or plane. Ambon is not an entry point for the electronic visa on arrival S21.

journeys.title: Asmara, the mountain railway and the Dahlak Islands
journeys.where: Asmara highlands, Massawa and the Dahlak Archipelago, Eritrea

season.note: Coast and sea set the window: Massawa about 30 °C Dec-Mar, about 40 °C May-Sep. Asmara is dry Oct-Mar. Fills March, which no other candidate covers.

journeys.pull: The trip goes in a sequence: a highland capital, an Italian mountain railway, a Red Sea port, then days offshore. Asmara is a planned colonial city, built in phases between 1893 and 1941, with its cinemas, shops and banks still intact. UNESCO's description stresses that Eritreans incorporated this colonial city into their own identity S1. The aircraft-winged Fiat Tagliero service station dates from 1938 S2 (unverified). The 950 mm railway was built down the escarpment between 1887 and 1932, and the 1938 Mallet steam locomotives still run S3 (unverified). From Massawa, boats go out to the Dahlak Archipelago to snorkel and camp.
journeys.journey: A concept, not an itinerary. Fly into Asmara: the dependable routes are via Dubai, Istanbul or Cairo, and all arrive after dark S21 (unverified). Spend three or four days walking Asmara, then take a chartered steam train down the escarpment. The section is disputed. An Asmara operator says Asmara to Arberebu and back, about 32 km round trip S4. A guide updated in August 2026 says Asmara to Nefasit S5 (unverified). A February 2026 photo charter ran out of Nefasit, but was then held above Arbaroba after lineside fires S6 (unverified). No public train runs to Massawa. The train is hired whole, so the group's size sets the cost per head. Drive down to Massawa for a night or two in the old port. Then spend two or three nights on the islands: an Asmara agency lists a three-day, two-night Dahlak trip S8, and a foreign operator runs two nights of camping S9 (unverified). Return to Asmara. That makes 9–14 days. Time worth protecting: unscheduled Asmara café and cinema hours, and a slack day on the coast for weather and permits.

journeys.title: Greenland by coastal ferry

season.note: Good months are still an estimate. The ship sails weekly through the end of 2027 (S1); the booking data read on 9 Oct lists port calls from August to November 2027, the months checked (S2). US flights ran only June-September in 2026 (S5).

journeys.pull: Sarfaq Ittuk is the scheduled passenger ship on Greenland's west coast, and its contract runs only to the end of 2027 S1. The trip would be a passage north from Nuuk past Maniitsoq, Sisimiut and Aasiaat to Ilulissat on the boat the coast itself uses, then time on Disko Bay. If the friends' window opens early enough in 2027, this may be the last year it can be done this way.
journeys.journey: Proposal, UNVERIFIED as a whole: fly to Nuuk, spend two or three nights there, and take the weekly sailing north. By a research agent's reading of the booking data the passage takes about 40 hours S3. Then three or four nights in Ilulissat, with day boats on Disko Bay, before flying out. The ship calls at Ilulissat once a week, so the passage north and the flight home must be built around that single call. Sailing both ways doubles the sea time and halves the time ashore.
questions: Does the friends' 2027 window include August or early September? On 2026 evidence, US–Nuuk flights stop in late September.

journeys.title: Ogasawara by the weekly ship

season.note: Inferred from the 2027 timetable (three-night stays from 24 Aug), whale seasons and typhoon normals.

journeys.pull: The only public way to the Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands is a 24-hour ship from Tokyo, and the ship's timetable sets the stay: from late August 2027, three nights on Chichijima, then the same ship home S1. The islands were settled in 1830 by a mixed group from Hawaii that included the American Nathaniel Savory S8. The United States administered them after 1945 and returned them to Japan in 1968 S9. Both of those history claims are unverified here.
journeys.journey:
One cycle is six days from Tokyo:
- Depart Takeshiba at 11:00 and arrive at Chichijima at 11:00 the next day.
- Three nights ashore.
- Leave at 15:00 and reach Tokyo at 15:00 the next day S1.
